content.title: About
content.content: The Burrito Bowl with chicken and beans is a Mexican‑inspired dish that combines rice, grilled chicken pieces, black or red beans, fresh vegetables, salsa and sour cream in a single bowl. It offers a balanced mix of protein, complex carbs and fiber for a satisfying meal.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The burrito bowl gained popularity in the United States in the early 2000s as a lighter alternative to the traditional wrapped burrito.
Chicken is usually seasoned with chipotle or other smoky spices, giving the bowl a distinctive flavor.
Beans provide a plant‑based source of protein and iron, and are often used in vegetarian versions of the bowl.
Traditional bowls use corn rice, but brown rice or quinoa can be substituted for added nutrition.
The dish is easily customized for dietary needs, such as swapping sour cream for guacamole or cheese for a vegan alternative.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Chicken supplies high‑quality animal protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Good source of fiber
items.content: Beans and vegetables add soluble and insoluble fiber, supporting digestive health.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Chicken and beans are rich in vitamin B6 and folate, which play key roles in energy metabolism.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Compared with traditional beef‑filled burritos, this bowl contains less saturated fat, benefiting heart health.

items.title: Antioxidants from veggies
items.content: Fresh tomatoes, peppers and salsa provide lycopene and vitamin C, protecting cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Chicken allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to chicken, experiencing skin reactions or digestive issues.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Salsa, sauces, and canned beans can be high in salt; people with hypertension should monitor portions.

items.title: Calorie density
items.content: Adding generous amounts of cheese, sour cream, or guacamole can make the bowl calorie‑rich.

items.title: Foodborne illness
items.content: Chicken must be cooked thoroughly to avoid the risk of salmonella.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the bowl in a deep plate or bowl. Mix the ingredients together, then drizzle your favorite sauce. It can be eaten with a fork or spoon, and topped with lime, guacamole, or crunchy tortilla chips for extra texture.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Prepared bowl can be kept in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. Store chicken and beans separate from fresh veggies to maintain crunch. When reheating, add a splash of water or sauce to prevent drying out.

content.title: About
content.content: Steamed whiting is a delicate white fish with low fat content and high-quality protein. Steaming preserves most of its nutrients, making it an excellent choice for healthy eating.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Whiting belongs to the cod family and is widely distributed in northern seas.
Steaming retains the fish’s natural flavor without adding extra fats.
Whiting is a good source of B‑group vitamins, especially B12, which supports the nervous system.
In the wild, whiting can grow over 100 cm, but culinary portions usually use smaller specimens.
Whiting is a traditional ingredient in Scandinavian and Russian cuisines.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Whiting provides complete protein needed for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Steamed whiting contains very little saturated fat, suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Rich in iodine
items.content: Iodine supports thyroid function and hormone production.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Vitamin B12 and B6 aid metabolism and nervous system health.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Whiting supplies selenium, phosphorus, and magnesium, important for bones and antioxidant protection.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to fish, including whiting.

items.title: Heavy‑metal contamination
items.content: In certain regions fish may contain traces of mercury or other heavy metals; choose reputable sources.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: If the fish is pre‑salted, consider its contribution to daily sodium intake.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Steamed whiting can be served as a main dish, added to salads, soups, or used in wraps. It pairs well with lemon, fresh herbs (dill, parsley) and light yogurt‑based sauces.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store fresh whiting in the refrigerator at 0‑2 °C in an airtight container for up to 2 days. Frozen fish can be kept at –18 °C for up to 3 months. Before cooking, check for any off‑odors.

content.title: About
content.content: Soft pretzels are a ready‑to‑eat, unsalted, butter‑free baked snack made from wheat flour, water, yeast and a pinch of salt. They have a mild flavor and a chewy texture, perfect for pairing with a variety of dips and toppings.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Soft pretzels originated in Germany, where they are known as "Brezel".
The iconic twisted shape is said to represent crossed arms in prayer.
In the United States they are commonly served with mustard, cheese sauce, or sweet glazes.
There are more than 200 pretzel varieties, including chocolate‑filled, cinnamon‑sugar, and nut‑topped versions.
Sales of ready‑to‑eat soft pretzels in Europe grew by over 12 % in the early 2020s.

items.title: Source of carbohydrates
items.content: Provides quick‑digesting carbs for an immediate energy boost.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Absence of butter makes them less calorie‑dense than many baked snacks.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Wheat flour supplies modest amounts of thiamine, riboflavin and niacin, supporting metabolism.

items.title: Plant protein
items.content: Each serving delivers about 5 g of protein, helping to promote satiety.

items.title: Easy to digest
items.content: Soft texture is gentle on the digestive system, suitable for children and seniors.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: Made from wheat flour, they are unsuitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Although unsalted, a small amount of sodium may be present in the recipe.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Can raise blood sugar quickly, so portion control is advised for diabetics.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy soft pretzels as a snack on their own, split them and spread with cream cheese, hummus, avocado, or sweet jam. They also serve as a base for mini sandwiches and appetizer bites.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 3‑4 days. For longer freshness, store in the refrigerator, where they stay soft for about a week.
